lines.s: You hear a woman talking about a course she did.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士談她上過的課程。
lines.en: You hear a woman talking about a course she did.

lines.s: I'd assumed a photography course would be mostly about cameras and settings, and of course there was some of that. But what really stayed with me was how much time we spent just looking — at light, at shapes, at people. I see things differently now, even without a camera in my hand.
lines.zh: 我原本以為攝影課主要是講相機和設定，當然也有一些。但真正讓我印象深刻的，是我們花了很多時間只是「看」——看光線、形狀、人。現在就算手上沒有相機，我看東西的方式也不一樣了。
lines.en: I'd assumed a photography course would be mostly about cameras and settings, and of course there was some of that. But what really stayed with me was how much time we spent just looking — at light, at shapes, at people. I see things differently now, even without a camera in my hand.

ask.s: What does she say about the course?
ask.en: What does she say about the course?

options.t: It changed the way she notices things.
It focused too much on technical details.
It was mainly about photographing people.

explain.zh: 真正讓她印象深刻的是學會「看」，「現在看東西的方式也不一樣了」。
explain.en: It changed how she sees things.

lines.s: You hear two friends talking about a new café.
lines.zh: 你聽到兩個朋友談一家新咖啡店。
lines.en: You hear two friends talking about a new café.

lines.s: Have you tried the new café on King Street?
lines.zh: 你去過國王街那家新咖啡店嗎？
lines.en: Have you tried the new café on King Street?

lines.s: Twice. The coffee's nothing special, but it's the only place round here where you can actually find a quiet table to work at.
lines.zh: 去過兩次。咖啡沒什麼特別，可是那是附近唯一真的能找到安靜位子工作的地方。
lines.en: Twice. The coffee's nothing special, but it's the only place round here where you can actually find a quiet table to work at.

lines.s: That's exactly what I need.
lines.zh: 那正是我需要的。
lines.en: That's exactly what I need.

ask.s: What do they both like about the café?
ask.zh: 他們兩個都喜歡這家咖啡店的什麼？
ask.en: What do they both like about the café?

options.t: the quality of the coffee
the low prices
the chance to work there in peace

explain.zh: 咖啡沒什麼特別，但「能找到安靜位子工作」，男的說「那正是我需要的」。

lines.s: You hear a man talking about his job as a tour guide.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談他當導遊的工作。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about his job as a tour guide.

lines.s: People think the difficult part is remembering all the history, but that's easy once you've done it a few times. What's hard is keeping a group of thirty tired tourists interested at four o'clock in the afternoon.
lines.zh: 大家以為最難的是記住所有歷史，其實帶過幾次就很簡單了。難的是在下午四點，讓一團三十個累壞的遊客保持興趣。
lines.en: People think the difficult part is remembering all the history, but that's easy once you've done it a few times. What's hard is keeping a group of thirty tired tourists interested at four o'clock in the afternoon.

ask.s: What does he find most challenging?
ask.zh: 他覺得最有挑戰的是什麼？
ask.en: What does he find most challenging?

options.t: learning historical facts
holding people's attention
organising large groups

explain.zh: 記歷史很簡單，難的是「讓累壞的遊客保持興趣」。

lines.s: You hear a student talking about choosing a university.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位學生談選大學。
lines.en: You hear a student talking about choosing a university.

lines.s: Everyone told me to choose the university with the best reputation. But when I visited, I just didn't feel comfortable there. The smaller one felt friendlier, and the course had more practical work, which is how I learn best. So that's where I'm going.
lines.zh: 大家都叫我選名氣最大的大學。可是我去參觀時，就是覺得不自在。比較小的那間感覺比較友善，課程也有比較多實作，那是我最好的學習方式。所以我要去那間。
lines.en: Everyone told me to choose the university with the best reputation. But when I visited, I just didn't feel comfortable there. The smaller one felt friendlier, and the course had more practical work, which is how I learn best. So that's where I'm going.

ask.s: Why did she choose the smaller university?
ask.zh: 她為什麼選比較小的大學？
ask.en: Why did she choose the smaller university?

options.t: Her friends were going there.
It had a better reputation.
The course suited her way of learning.

explain.zh: 「課程有比較多實作，那是我最好的學習方式」。
explain.en: More practical work suits how she learns.

lines.s: You hear a man leaving a voicemail for a colleague.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士給同事留語音訊息。
lines.en: You hear a man leaving a voicemail for a colleague.

lines.s: Hi Sarah, it's Mike. About tomorrow's presentation — I've finished the slides, but I'm not happy with the figures in section three. Could you check them before you send everything to the client? I don't want them to see any mistakes.
lines.zh: 莎拉，我是麥克。關於明天的簡報，投影片我做好了，但我對第三部分的數字不太放心。你寄給客戶之前可以幫我檢查一下嗎？我不想讓他們看到錯誤。
lines.en: Hi Sarah, it's Mike. About tomorrow's presentation — I've finished the slides, but I'm not happy with the figures in section three. Could you check them before you send everything to the client? I don't want them to see any mistakes.

ask.s: What does Mike want Sarah to do?
ask.en: What does Mike want Sarah to do?

options.t: check some information
finish the slides
contact the client today

explain.zh: 「你寄給客戶之前可以幫我檢查一下嗎」：檢查第三部分的數字。

lines.s: You hear a woman talking about moving to the countryside.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士談搬到鄉下。
lines.en: You hear a woman talking about moving to the countryside.

lines.s: I expected to miss the shops and restaurants, and I don't at all. What I hadn't expected was how dark it gets at night. In the city, there's always some light. Here, without a torch, you can't see your own hand.
lines.zh: 我以為自己會想念商店和餐廳，結果完全不會。我沒料到的是晚上會這麼暗。在城市裡總有一點光，這裡沒有手電筒，連自己的手都看不見。
lines.en: I expected to miss the shops and restaurants, and I don't at all. What I hadn't expected was how dark it gets at night. In the city, there's always some light. Here, without a torch, you can't see your own hand.

ask.s: What surprised her about living in the countryside?
ask.zh: 住在鄉下讓她意外的是什麼？
ask.en: What surprised her about living in the countryside?

options.t: how much she missed the city
how dark the nights are
how far it is to the shops

explain.zh: 「我沒料到的是晚上會這麼暗」；她並不想念商店。
explain.en: How dark it gets at night.

lines.s: You hear two colleagues talking about a meeting.
lines.zh: 你聽到兩位同事談一場會議。
lines.en: You hear two colleagues talking about a meeting.

lines.s: That meeting went on for two hours and we still didn't decide anything.
lines.zh: 那個會開了兩個小時，結果什麼都沒決定。
lines.en: That meeting went on for two hours and we still didn't decide anything.

lines.s: I know. Next time, we should send everyone the agenda the day before, so people come prepared.
lines.zh: 我知道。下次我們應該前一天把議程寄給大家，讓大家有準備再來。
lines.en: I know. Next time, we should send everyone the agenda the day before, so people come prepared.

ask.s: What does the man suggest?
ask.en: What does the man suggest?

options.t: having shorter meetings
inviting fewer people
giving people information in advance

explain.zh: 「前一天把議程寄給大家」：事先給資訊。
explain.en: Send the agenda the day before.

lines.s: You hear a man talking about learning to cook.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談學做菜。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about learning to cook.

lines.s: I followed recipes exactly for years and never really understood why they worked. Then a friend told me to stop measuring everything and taste as I go. It sounds obvious, but it completely changed my cooking.
lines.zh: 我多年來都完全照食譜做，從來不懂為什麼這樣做會好吃。後來一個朋友叫我別再什麼都量，邊煮邊嚐。聽起來理所當然，卻徹底改變了我的廚藝。
lines.en: I followed recipes exactly for years and never really understood why they worked. Then a friend told me to stop measuring everything and taste as I go. It sounds obvious, but it completely changed my cooking.

ask.s: What helped him to cook better?
ask.zh: 什麼幫他把菜做得更好？
ask.en: What helped him to cook better?

options.t: tasting the food while cooking
following recipes carefully
taking a cookery course

explain.zh: 朋友叫他「邊煮邊嚐」，徹底改變了他的廚藝。

lines.s: Hello, I'm Dr Anna Kerr, and I study sleep. I'm often asked how much sleep people really need. For most adults, the answer is between seven and nine hours, although teenagers need more — around nine. One of the biggest problems today is light from screens. It tells the brain that it's still daytime, so it delays the release of melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy. My advice is to switch off phones at least an hour before bed. Temperature matters too: a bedroom should be cool, ideally around eighteen degrees. Many people believe that a glass of wine helps them sleep. In fact, alcohol reduces the quality of sleep in the second half of the night. And if you can't sleep, don't lie there worrying — get up, go to another room and read something until you feel tired. Finally, try to wake up at the same time every day, even at weekends. Your body clock will thank you.
lines.zh: 大家好，我是安娜·柯爾博士，研究睡眠。常有人問我，人到底需要睡多久。大多數成人是七到九小時，不過青少年需要更多，大約九小時。現在最大的問題之一是螢幕的光。它告訴大腦現在還是白天，所以會延遲褪黑激素的分泌，那是讓我們想睡的荷爾蒙。我的建議是睡前至少一小時關掉手機。溫度也很重要：臥室應該涼一點，最好大約十八度。很多人以為喝一杯酒有助睡眠，其實酒精會降低後半夜的睡眠品質。如果睡不著，不要躺著擔心——起床到另一個房間看點東西，直到覺得累。最後，試著每天在同一時間起床，週末也一樣，你的生理時鐘會感謝你。
lines.en: Hello, I'm Dr Anna Kerr, and I study sleep. I'm often asked how much sleep people really need. For most adults, the answer is between seven and nine hours, although teenagers need more — around nine. One of the biggest problems today is light from screens. It tells the brain that it's still daytime, so it delays the release of melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy. My advice is to switch off phones at least an hour before bed. Temperature matters too: a bedroom should be cool, ideally around eighteen degrees. Many people believe that a glass of wine helps them sleep. In fact, alcohol reduces the quality of sleep in the second half of the night. And if you can't sleep, don't lie there worrying — get up, go to another room and read something until you feel tired. Finally, try to wake up at the same time every day, even at weekends. Your body clock will thank you.

lines.s: I started playing the guitar at forty, which people find funny. My teacher said it would take years to sound decent, but within six months I was playing songs I'd loved since I was a teenager. I honestly couldn't believe it.
lines.zh: 我四十歲才開始彈吉他，大家覺得很好笑。老師說要好幾年才能彈得像樣，可是六個月內我就能彈從青少年時期就喜歡的歌。我真的不敢相信。
lines.en: I started playing the guitar at forty, which people find funny. My teacher said it would take years to sound decent, but within six months I was playing songs I'd loved since I was a teenager. I honestly couldn't believe it.

lines.s: Speaker 2
lines.zh: 說話者 2
lines.en: Speaker 2

lines.s: My grandfather was a carpenter, and he taught me to make furniture in his workshop when I was small. Now I build tables and chairs at the weekend. Every time I pick up his old tools, I think of him.
lines.zh: 我爺爺是木匠，我小時候他在工作室教我做家具。現在我週末會做桌椅。每次拿起他留下的舊工具，我都會想起他。
lines.en: My grandfather was a carpenter, and he taught me to make furniture in his workshop when I was small. Now I build tables and chairs at the weekend. Every time I pick up his old tools, I think of him.

lines.s: I joined a running club after I moved to a new city and didn't know anyone. Now my closest friends are people I met there. We still run together twice a week, and we usually go for breakfast afterwards.
lines.zh: 我搬到新城市、誰都不認識，就加入了跑步社。現在我最好的朋友都是在那裡認識的。我們還是每週一起跑兩次，跑完通常一起吃早餐。
lines.en: I joined a running club after I moved to a new city and didn't know anyone. Now my closest friends are people I met there. We still run together twice a week, and we usually go for breakfast afterwards.

lines.en: I took up painting because my job is so stressful. I'm not very good, and I don't really care. For two hours every Sunday, I forget about work completely. That's the whole point for me.

lines.s: My guest today is Clara Webb, a wildlife filmmaker whose latest series follows wolves in Canada. Clara, how did you get into this kind of work?
lines.zh: 今天的來賓是野生動物紀錄片導演克拉拉·韋伯，她最新的影集記錄加拿大的狼。克拉拉，你怎麼會走進這一行？
lines.en: My guest today is Clara Webb, a wildlife filmmaker whose latest series follows wolves in Canada. Clara, how did you get into this kind of work?

lines.s: Completely by accident. I was studying biology and volunteered to help a film crew carry equipment for a week. I expected to be bored, but watching how they told a story with animals was fascinating. I changed my plans after that.
lines.zh: 完全是意外。我當時讀生物，自願幫一個攝影團隊搬一週的器材。我以為會很無聊，結果看他們怎麼用動物說故事，覺得非常迷人。從那之後我就改變了計畫。
lines.en: Completely by accident. I was studying biology and volunteered to help a film crew carry equipment for a week. I expected to be bored, but watching how they told a story with animals was fascinating. I changed my plans after that.

lines.s: Your new series took three years to film. Why so long?
lines.zh: 你的新影集拍了三年，為什麼這麼久？
lines.en: Your new series took three years to film. Why so long?

lines.s: Wolves are extremely shy, so for the first year we hardly saw them at all. We had to let them get used to our presence. People imagine the hard part is the cold, but it's really the patience.
lines.zh: 狼非常怕生，所以第一年我們幾乎看不到牠們。我們得讓牠們習慣我們的存在。大家以為最難的是寒冷，其實真正難的是耐心。
lines.en: Wolves are extremely shy, so for the first year we hardly saw them at all. We had to let them get used to our presence. People imagine the hard part is the cold, but it's really the patience.

lines.s: Some viewers have said the series makes wolves look too friendly. What's your response?
lines.zh: 有些觀眾說這部影集把狼拍得太友善了，你怎麼回應？
lines.en: Some viewers have said the series makes wolves look too friendly. What's your response?

lines.s: I understand the concern, but we never changed what happened. Wolves are often shown as monsters, and I wanted to show them as family animals, which they are. That doesn't mean they aren't dangerous.
lines.zh: 我理解這個擔心，但我們從沒改動實際發生的事。狼常被描繪成怪物，我想呈現牠們是重視家庭的動物，而牠們確實是。這不代表牠們不危險。
lines.en: I understand the concern, but we never changed what happened. Wolves are often shown as monsters, and I wanted to show them as family animals, which they are. That doesn't mean they aren't dangerous.

lines.s: What do you hope people take away from it?
lines.zh: 你希望觀眾從中得到什麼？
lines.en: What do you hope people take away from it?

lines.s: Mostly, I'd like them to question what they think they know. If one person watches it and decides to find out more, that's enough for me.
lines.zh: 我最希望大家質疑自己以為知道的事。只要有一個人看完後決定去多了解一些，對我來說就夠了。
lines.en: Mostly, I'd like them to question what they think they know. If one person watches it and decides to find out more, that's enough for me.

ask.s: How did Clara become a wildlife filmmaker?
ask.zh: 克拉拉怎麼成為野生動物紀錄片導演的？
ask.en: How did Clara become a wildlife filmmaker?

A biology teacher encouraged her.

explain.zh: 自願幫攝影團隊搬一週器材，「從那之後我就改變了計畫」。
explain.en: A week helping a film crew changed her plans.

ask.s: What did she expect before working with the film crew?
ask.zh: 和攝影團隊工作前，她預期會怎樣？
ask.en: What did she expect before working with the film crew?

options.t: that she would find it dull
that it would be dangerous
that she would learn a lot

explain.zh: 「我以為會很無聊」。

ask.s: Why did the series take three years to film?
ask.en: Why did the series take three years to film?

options.t: The weather was very bad.
The crew was very small.
The wolves needed time to accept the crew.

explain.zh: 狼很怕生，「我們得讓牠們習慣我們的存在」。
explain.en: The wolves had to get used to them.

ask.s: What does Clara say was the hardest part?
ask.zh: 克拉拉說最難的是什麼？
ask.en: What does Clara say was the hardest part?

options.t: the cold
being patient
carrying the equipment

explain.zh: 「大家以為最難的是寒冷，其實真正難的是耐心」。

ask.s: How does Clara respond to the criticism of the series?
ask.zh: 克拉拉怎麼回應對影集的批評？
ask.en: How does Clara respond to the criticism of the series?

options.t: She says the events were shown truthfully.
She admits she made the wolves look friendly.
She says wolves are not dangerous.

explain.zh: 「我們從沒改動實際發生的事」；她也說這不代表狼不危險。
explain.en: Nothing was changed; wolves can still be dangerous.

ask.s: How does Clara describe wolves?
ask.en: How does Clara describe wolves?

options.t: as monsters
as easy to film
as animals that care about their families

explain.zh: 「我想呈現牠們是重視家庭的動物，而牠們確實是」。

ask.s: What does Clara hope viewers will do?
ask.zh: 克拉拉希望觀眾怎麼做？
ask.en: What does Clara hope viewers will do?

options.t: visit Canada
think again about what they believe
support wildlife charities

explain.zh: 「我最希望大家質疑自己以為知道的事」。
explain.en: Question what they think they know.

lines.s: You hear a man talking about working from home.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談在家工作。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about working from home.

lines.s: Everyone warned me that working from home would be lonely, and I was prepared for that. What I wasn't ready for was how hard it is to stop. My office is my kitchen table, so I end up answering emails at ten at night.
lines.zh: 大家都警告我在家工作會很孤單，這我有心理準備。我沒料到的是停下來有多難。我的辦公室就是廚房的餐桌，所以我常常晚上十點還在回信。
lines.en: Everyone warned me that working from home would be lonely, and I was prepared for that. What I wasn't ready for was how hard it is to stop. My office is my kitchen table, so I end up answering emails at ten at night.

ask.s: What has he found difficult?
ask.en: What has he found difficult?

options.t: feeling lonely
knowing when to finish work
having no space to work

explain.zh: 孤單他早有準備，沒料到的是「停下來有多難」，晚上十點還在回信。
explain.en: He was ready for loneliness; stopping work is the problem.

lines.s: You hear two friends talking about a film.
lines.zh: 你聽到兩個朋友談一部電影。
lines.en: You hear two friends talking about a film.

lines.s: I thought the ending was a bit disappointing.
lines.zh: 我覺得結局有點讓人失望。
lines.en: I thought the ending was a bit disappointing.

lines.s: Really? I thought it was the best part. It's the beginning that drags — nothing happens for forty minutes.
lines.zh: 真的嗎？我覺得那是最精彩的部分。拖戲的是開頭，前四十分鐘什麼事都沒發生。
lines.en: Really? I thought it was the best part. It's the beginning that drags — nothing happens for forty minutes.

lines.s: Hmm, that's fair.
lines.zh: 嗯，這倒是。
lines.en: Hmm, that's fair.

ask.s: What do they agree about?
ask.en: What do they agree about?

options.t: The ending was excellent.
The film was too short.
The start of the film was slow.

explain.zh: 結局兩人看法不同；男的說開頭拖戲，女的回「這倒是」：同意開頭太慢。
explain.en: They disagree on the ending; she agrees the start drags.

lines.s: You hear a woman talking about a hotel.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士談一家飯店。
lines.en: You hear a woman talking about a hotel.

lines.s: The room itself was tiny, but that didn't bother me — I was hardly in it. What made the stay was the staff. Nothing was too much trouble; they even found me a doctor at midnight when I was ill.
lines.zh: 房間本身很小，不過我不在意，我幾乎都不在房裡。讓這次住宿加分的是員工。什麼要求都不嫌麻煩，我半夜生病時他們甚至幫我找了醫生。
lines.en: The room itself was tiny, but that didn't bother me — I was hardly in it. What made the stay was the staff. Nothing was too much trouble; they even found me a doctor at midnight when I was ill.

ask.s: What did she value most about the hotel?
ask.zh: 她最看重這家飯店的什麼？
ask.en: What did she value most about the hotel?

options.t: the helpful staff
the size of the room
its location

explain.zh: 「讓這次住宿加分的是員工」，半夜還幫她找醫生。

lines.s: You hear a man talking about learning to swim as an adult.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談成年後學游泳。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about learning to swim as an adult.

lines.s: I'd always told people I didn't like water. The truth is, I was embarrassed. When I finally booked lessons, I chose an early-morning class so that nobody I knew would see me.
lines.zh: 我一直跟別人說我不喜歡水。其實是我覺得丟臉。我終於報名上課時，選了一大早的班，這樣就不會被認識的人看到。
lines.en: I'd always told people I didn't like water. The truth is, I was embarrassed. When I finally booked lessons, I chose an early-morning class so that nobody I knew would see me.

ask.s: Why did he choose an early-morning class?
ask.zh: 他為什麼選一大早的班？
ask.en: Why did he choose an early-morning class?

options.t: It was cheaper.
It fitted in with his work.
He didn't want to be seen.

explain.zh: 選早班是「這樣就不會被認識的人看到」。
explain.en: So nobody he knew would see him.

lines.s: You hear a student talking to her teacher about a project.
lines.zh: 你聽到一個學生和老師談作業。
lines.en: You hear a student talking to her teacher about a project.

lines.s: I've finished the research, but I'm struggling to organise it. I've got far too much information, and I don't know what to leave out.
lines.zh: 我已經查完資料了，可是不知道怎麼整理。我的資料太多了，不知道該刪掉哪些。
lines.en: I've finished the research, but I'm struggling to organise it. I've got far too much information, and I don't know what to leave out.

ask.s: What is her problem?
ask.en: What is her problem?

options.t: She hasn't found enough information.
She can't decide what to include.
She has missed the deadline.

explain.zh: 資料太多，「不知道該刪掉哪些」：決定不了要放什麼。
explain.en: Too much information; she cannot decide what to leave out.

lines.s: You hear a woman talking about the restaurant she owns.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士談她開的餐廳。
lines.en: You hear a woman talking about the restaurant she owns.

lines.s: When we opened, we tried to please everybody — pizza, curry, burgers. It was a disaster. Now we serve twelve dishes, all from my mother's region of Italy, and we're full every night.
lines.zh: 剛開的時候我們想討好每個人，披薩、咖哩、漢堡都賣，結果一團糟。現在我們只賣十二道菜，全是我媽媽家鄉義大利那一區的菜，每天晚上都客滿。
lines.en: When we opened, we tried to please everybody — pizza, curry, burgers. It was a disaster. Now we serve twelve dishes, all from my mother's region of Italy, and we're full every night.

ask.s: What led to the restaurant's success?
ask.zh: 餐廳成功的原因是什麼？
ask.en: What led to the restaurant's success?

options.t: offering fewer, more focused dishes
lowering its prices
advertising online

explain.zh: 什麼都賣很失敗，改成只賣十二道家鄉菜後天天客滿。
explain.en: Twelve dishes from one region instead of everything.

lines.s: You hear two colleagues talking about a meeting.
lines.zh: 你聽到兩位同事談一場會議。
lines.en: You hear two colleagues talking about a meeting.

lines.s: That meeting was a waste of time.
lines.zh: 那場會議根本是浪費時間。
lines.en: That meeting was a waste of time.

lines.s: I know. We spent an hour discussing the problem and didn't agree on a single solution.
lines.zh: 我知道。討論問題花了一個小時，連一個解決辦法都沒談定。
lines.en: I know. We spent an hour discussing the problem and didn't agree on a single solution.

lines.s: Next time, someone should prepare some options beforehand.
lines.zh: 下次應該有人事先準備幾個方案。
lines.en: Next time, someone should prepare some options beforehand.

ask.s: What does the man suggest?
ask.en: What does the man suggest?

options.t: holding shorter meetings
having proposals ready in advance
inviting fewer people

explain.zh: 「下次應該有人事先準備幾個方案」。

lines.s: You hear a man talking about a novel he has read.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談他讀過的一本小說。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about a novel he has read.

lines.s: I almost gave up after the first chapter — the writing seemed so plain. But gradually I realised that was the point. The simple language makes the terrible events even more powerful.
lines.zh: 看完第一章我差點放棄，文字顯得太平淡了。可是慢慢地我發現那正是重點：簡單的文字讓那些可怕的事件更有力量。
lines.en: I almost gave up after the first chapter — the writing seemed so plain. But gradually I realised that was the point. The simple language makes the terrible events even more powerful.

ask.s: What does he say about the writing?
ask.zh: 他怎麼說這本書的文字？
ask.en: What does he say about the writing?

options.t: It was too complicated.
It was dull all the way through.
Its simplicity made the story stronger.

explain.zh: 「簡單的文字讓那些可怕的事件更有力量」。
explain.en: The plain language makes the events more powerful.

lines.s: Hi, I'm Freya, and for the last six years I've worked as a guide on volcanoes in Iceland. People often think I must have studied geology, but in fact my degree was in history. I started as a summer assistant at a hotel and was asked to help on a tour when one of the guides fell ill. The tours usually last about five hours, and most of that time is spent walking across lava fields. The most important piece of equipment isn't a helmet — it's a good pair of boots, because the rock is incredibly sharp. Before every tour, we check readings from the national weather office, since gas levels can change quickly. The hardest part of the job is actually the wind, which can be strong enough to knock you over. The best moment, for me, is when visitors see the glow of lava for the first time — most of them go completely silent. In winter there are fewer tours, so I spend those months teaching first aid. Next year I'm hoping to start my own small company, offering tours for photographers.
lines.zh: 大家好，我是芙蕾雅，過去六年在冰島當火山嚮導。大家常以為我一定是讀地質的，其實我的學位是歷史。我一開始在一家飯店當暑期助理，有一次一位嚮導生病，他們請我幫忙帶團。行程通常大約五個小時，大部分時間都在熔岩原上走。最重要的裝備不是安全帽，而是一雙好鞋，因為岩石非常尖銳。每次出團前，我們都會查看國家氣象局的數據，因為氣體濃度變化很快。這份工作最難的其實是風，強到能把人吹倒。對我來說最棒的時刻，是遊客第一次看到熔岩發出的紅光，大部分人都會完全安靜下來。冬天行程比較少，所以那幾個月我教急救。明年我希望開一家自己的小公司，專門帶攝影師的團。
lines.en: Hi, I'm Freya, and for the last six years I've worked as a guide on volcanoes in Iceland. People often think I must have studied geology, but in fact my degree was in history. I started as a summer assistant at a hotel and was asked to help on a tour when one of the guides fell ill. The tours usually last about five hours, and most of that time is spent walking across lava fields. The most important piece of equipment isn't a helmet — it's a good pair of boots, because the rock is incredibly sharp. Before every tour, we check readings from the national weather office, since gas levels can change quickly. The hardest part of the job is actually the wind, which can be strong enough to knock you over. The best moment, for me, is when visitors see the glow of lava for the first time — most of them go completely silent. In winter there are fewer tours, so I spend those months teaching first aid. Next year I'm hoping to start my own small company, offering tours for photographers.

ask.en: Guides check readings from the national ＿＿＿＿＿ office.

ask.en: The hardest part of the job is the ＿＿＿＿＿.

explain.zh: 「最難的其實是風」。

ask.zh: 第一次看到熔岩紅光，大部分遊客會變得＿＿。
ask.en: When they first see the lava glow, most visitors go ＿＿＿＿＿.

explain.zh: 「大部分人都會完全安靜下來」。

ask.en: In winter she teaches ＿＿＿＿＿.

explain.zh: 「那幾個月我教急救」。

ask.en: She plans to offer tours for ＿＿＿＿＿.

lines.en: Speaker 1

lines.s: I moved to Lisbon for a job, and the first month was miserable. It rained every day, my flat was cold, and I didn't know a soul. I'd actually booked a flight home when a colleague invited me to a party, and everything changed after that.
lines.zh: 我為了工作搬到里斯本，第一個月過得很悲慘。每天下雨，公寓很冷，一個人也不認識。我其實都訂好回家的機票了，結果一位同事邀我去派對，從那之後一切都變了。
lines.en: I moved to Lisbon for a job, and the first month was miserable. It rained every day, my flat was cold, and I didn't know a soul. I'd actually booked a flight home when a colleague invited me to a party, and everything changed after that.

lines.zh: 說話者 2
lines.en: Speaker 2

lines.s: I went to Japan to teach English for a year, planning to come back and work in finance. But I became so interested in teaching that I did a master's in education instead. I've been a teacher ever since.
lines.zh: 我去日本教一年英文，本來打算回來做金融業。可是我對教書太有興趣，就改讀了教育碩士。之後就一直當老師。
lines.en: I went to Japan to teach English for a year, planning to come back and work in finance. But I became so interested in teaching that I did a master's in education instead. I've been a teacher ever since.

lines.s: Speaker 3
lines.zh: 說話者 3
lines.en: Speaker 3

lines.s: When I arrived in Mexico, the couple who lived downstairs more or less adopted me. They showed me where to shop, corrected my Spanish and invited me for lunch every Sunday.
lines.zh: 我到墨西哥時，住樓下的一對夫婦幾乎把我當自己的孩子照顧。他們帶我去買東西、糾正我的西班牙文，每個星期天都請我吃午餐。
lines.en: When I arrived in Mexico, the couple who lived downstairs more or less adopted me. They showed me where to shop, corrected my Spanish and invited me for lunch every Sunday.

lines.s: Speaker 4
lines.zh: 說話者 4
lines.en: Speaker 4

lines.s: I spent six months in Norway as a student. It went so fast. I'd only just started to feel at home when it was time to leave, and I've regretted not extending my stay ever since.
lines.zh: 我當學生時在挪威待了六個月，時間過得好快。我才剛開始覺得像家，就得離開了，從那之後我一直後悔沒有延長。
lines.en: I spent six months in Norway as a student. It went so fast. I'd only just started to feel at home when it was time to leave, and I've regretted not extending my stay ever since.

lines.s: Speaker 5
lines.zh: 說話者 5
lines.en: Speaker 5

lines.s: I'd studied German for years at school, so I thought I'd be fine in Berlin. But people spoke so fast, and used so much slang, that I could barely follow a conversation for the first six months.
lines.zh: 我在學校學了好幾年德文，以為到柏林沒問題。可是大家講話好快，又一堆俚語，前六個月我幾乎跟不上對話。
lines.en: I'd studied German for years at school, so I thought I'd be fine in Berlin. But people spoke so fast, and used so much slang, that I could barely follow a conversation for the first six months.

lines.s: My guest today is Jade Okafor, whose mobile game about looking after a forest has been downloaded ten million times. Jade, where did the idea come from?
lines.zh: 今天的來賓是潔德·奧卡福，她做的照顧森林手機遊戲已經被下載一千萬次。潔德，點子是從哪來的？
lines.en: My guest today is Jade Okafor, whose mobile game about looking after a forest has been downloaded ten million times. Jade, where did the idea come from?

lines.s: From my little brother, actually. He was obsessed with games where you destroy things, and I wondered whether a game about growing things could be just as exciting. I made the first version for him as a birthday present.
lines.zh: 其實是我弟弟。他超迷那種破壞東西的遊戲，我就想，一個讓東西成長的遊戲能不能一樣刺激。第一版是做給他當生日禮物的。
lines.en: From my little brother, actually. He was obsessed with games where you destroy things, and I wondered whether a game about growing things could be just as exciting. I made the first version for him as a birthday present.

lines.s: Did you have any training in game design?
lines.zh: 你受過遊戲設計的訓練嗎？
lines.en: Did you have any training in game design?

lines.s: Not really. I studied mathematics, which helped more than you'd think — a lot of game design is about balancing numbers. Everything else I learnt from online videos.
lines.zh: 其實沒有。我讀數學，這比你想的更有幫助，遊戲設計很多是在平衡數字。其他的都是看網路影片學的。
lines.en: Not really. I studied mathematics, which helped more than you'd think — a lot of game design is about balancing numbers. Everything else I learnt from online videos.

lines.s: The game has no adverts, which is unusual. Why is that?
lines.zh: 這個遊戲沒有廣告，很少見。為什麼？
lines.en: The game has no adverts, which is unusual. Why is that?

lines.s: I hate being interrupted when I'm playing. Instead, players can pay a small amount for extra trees, but you can finish the whole game without spending anything.
lines.zh: 我玩遊戲時最討厭被打斷。所以玩家可以花一點錢買額外的樹，不過一毛不花也能破完整個遊戲。
lines.en: I hate being interrupted when I'm playing. Instead, players can pay a small amount for extra trees, but you can finish the whole game without spending anything.

lines.s: What surprised you most after it came out?
lines.zh: 遊戲推出後，最讓你意外的是什麼？
lines.en: What surprised you most after it came out?

lines.s: How many older people play it. I'd assumed the players would be teenagers, but a third of them are over sixty. Lots of them write to me about their real gardens.
lines.zh: 有那麼多年紀大的人在玩。我原本以為玩家會是青少年，結果有三分之一超過六十歲。很多人寫信跟我聊他們真正的花園。
lines.en: How many older people play it. I'd assumed the players would be teenagers, but a third of them are over sixty. Lots of them write to me about their real gardens.

lines.s: Has success changed your life?
lines.zh: 成功改變了你的生活嗎？
lines.en: Has success changed your life?

lines.s: I've been able to hire four people, which is wonderful. But I still work from my kitchen table — I'm not ready for a proper office yet.
lines.zh: 我請得起四個人了，這很棒。不過我還是在廚房餐桌上工作，還沒準備好要有正式的辦公室。
lines.en: I've been able to hire four people, which is wonderful. But I still work from my kitchen table — I'm not ready for a proper office yet.

lines.s: What's next?
lines.zh: 接下來呢？
lines.en: What's next?

lines.s: A game about the ocean. Part of the money it makes will go to groups that clean up beaches.
lines.zh: 一個關於海洋的遊戲。它賺的錢有一部分會捐給淨灘團體。
lines.en: A game about the ocean. Part of the money it makes will go to groups that clean up beaches.

ask.s: Where did the idea for the game come from?
ask.en: Where did the idea for the game come from?

options.t: a game she played as a child
her brother's taste in games
a school project

explain.zh: 弟弟迷破壞東西的遊戲，她想做一個讓東西成長的遊戲給他。
explain.en: Her brother loved games about destroying things.

ask.s: What does Jade say about her studies?
ask.zh: 潔德怎麼說她讀的科系？
ask.en: What does Jade say about her studies?

options.t: They were useful for designing games.
She studied game design.
She left university early.

explain.zh: 讀數學「比你想的更有幫助」，遊戲設計很多是平衡數字。

ask.s: Why doesn't the game have adverts?
ask.en: Why doesn't the game have adverts?

options.t: They cost too much.
She dislikes being interrupted.
Players complained about them.

explain.zh: 「我玩遊戲時最討厭被打斷」。

ask.s: How does the game make money?
ask.en: How does the game make money?

options.t: Players pay to download it.
A company sponsors it.
Players can buy extra items.

explain.zh: 「玩家可以花一點錢買額外的樹」。
explain.en: Players can pay for extra trees.

ask.s: What surprised Jade?
ask.en: What surprised Jade?

options.t: the age of many players
the number of downloads
the cost of making the game

explain.zh: 以為玩家是青少年，結果「三分之一超過六十歲」。
explain.en: A third of players are over sixty.

ask.s: What does Jade say about her work now?
ask.zh: 潔德怎麼說她現在的工作？
ask.en: What does Jade say about her work now?

options.t: She has moved into an office.
She still works at home.
She works alone.

explain.zh: 「我還是在廚房餐桌上工作」；她請了四個人，所以不是一個人。
explain.en: Still at her kitchen table; she has four staff.

ask.s: What will happen with the ocean game?
ask.en: What will happen with the ocean game?

options.t: It will be free.
It will be made for teenagers.
Some of its money will support beach clean-ups.

explain.zh: 「賺的錢有一部分會捐給淨灘團體」。
explain.en: Part of the money goes to beach clean-ups.

lines.s: You hear a woman talking about a museum visit.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士談參觀博物館。
lines.en: You hear a woman talking about a museum visit.

lines.s: I'd gone to see the famous paintings, but honestly, the rooms were so crowded I could hardly see them. What I'll remember is the small exhibition of children's drawings downstairs — nobody else was there, and they were wonderful.
lines.zh: 我是去看那些名畫的，可是老實說展間擠到我幾乎看不到。我會記得的是樓下一個兒童畫的小展覽，沒有別人在，那些畫很棒。
lines.en: I'd gone to see the famous paintings, but honestly, the rooms were so crowded I could hardly see them. What I'll remember is the small exhibition of children's drawings downstairs — nobody else was there, and they were wonderful.

ask.s: What did she enjoy most?
ask.en: What did she enjoy most?

options.t: an exhibition few people visited
the famous paintings
the guided tour

explain.zh: 名畫太擠看不到，她會記得的是「沒有別人在」的兒童畫展。
explain.en: The quiet exhibition of children's drawings.

lines.s: You hear two friends talking about a concert.
lines.zh: 你聽到兩個朋友談一場演唱會。
lines.en: You hear two friends talking about a concert.

lines.s: The band sounded great, but the tickets were ridiculous.
lines.zh: 樂團的聲音很棒，可是票價太誇張了。
lines.en: The band sounded great, but the tickets were ridiculous.

lines.s: They were expensive, yes. My problem was the venue — we were so far from the stage.
lines.zh: 是很貴沒錯。我的問題是場地，我們離舞台好遠。
lines.en: They were expensive, yes. My problem was the venue — we were so far from the stage.

lines.s: True, we could barely see anything.
lines.zh: 對，我們幾乎什麼都看不到。
lines.en: True, we could barely see anything.

ask.s: What do they both complain about?
ask.en: What do they both complain about?

options.t: the sound
the price of the tickets
their view of the stage

explain.zh: 女的說離舞台太遠，男的附和「幾乎什麼都看不到」。票價只有男的提。
explain.en: Both say they could barely see; only he mentions the price.

lines.s: You hear a man talking about giving up sugar.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談戒糖。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about giving up sugar.

lines.s: Everyone said I'd feel more energetic, and maybe I do a bit. But what I didn't expect was that fruit would start tasting so sweet. An apple is like a dessert now.
lines.zh: 大家都說我會更有精神，也許有一點吧。但我沒料到水果會變得這麼甜。現在一顆蘋果就像甜點一樣。
lines.en: Everyone said I'd feel more energetic, and maybe I do a bit. But what I didn't expect was that fruit would start tasting so sweet. An apple is like a dessert now.

ask.s: What surprised him?
ask.en: What surprised him?

options.t: He had more energy.
Fruit tasted much sweeter.
He lost weight quickly.

explain.zh: 「我沒料到水果會變得這麼甜」；更有精神是大家早就說過的。
explain.en: Fruit tasting so sweet; the energy was expected.

lines.s: You hear a woman leaving a phone message.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士留電話留言。
lines.en: You hear a woman leaving a phone message.

lines.s: Hi Sam, it's Kate from the dentist's. Your appointment on Thursday is still at ten, but Dr Lewis is away, so you'll be seeing Dr Patel instead. No need to call back.
lines.zh: 山姆你好，我是牙醫診所的凱特。你星期四的預約還是十點，不過路易斯醫師不在，所以會改由帕特爾醫師看診。不用回電。
lines.en: Hi Sam, it's Kate from the dentist's. Your appointment on Thursday is still at ten, but Dr Lewis is away, so you'll be seeing Dr Patel instead. No need to call back.

ask.s: Why is she calling?
ask.en: Why is she calling?

options.t: to tell Sam about a change of dentist
to change the time of an appointment
to cancel an appointment

explain.zh: 時間「還是十點」，只是改由另一位醫師看診。

lines.s: You hear a teacher talking to a class.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位老師對全班說話。
lines.en: You hear a teacher talking to a class.

lines.s: Before you hand in your essays, check them once more. I'm not worried about your ideas — they're good — but some of you are still writing very long sentences that are hard to follow.
lines.zh: 交作文之前再檢查一次。我不擔心你們的想法，想法都不錯，可是有些人還是寫很長、很難讀懂的句子。
lines.en: Before you hand in your essays, check them once more. I'm not worried about your ideas — they're good — but some of you are still writing very long sentences that are hard to follow.

ask.s: What does the teacher want them to improve?
ask.zh: 老師希望他們改進什麼？
ask.en: What does the teacher want them to improve?

options.t: their ideas
their spelling
the length of their sentences

explain.zh: 想法不錯，問題是「很長、很難讀懂的句子」。

lines.s: You hear a man talking about a holiday.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談一次假期。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about a holiday.

lines.s: We'd booked a beach holiday, but there was a storm the whole week. So we hired a car and explored the mountains instead. Honestly, it was better than the beach would have been.
lines.zh: 我們訂的是海灘假期，結果整週都是暴風雨。所以我們租了車去山裡玩。老實說，比待在海灘還好。
lines.en: We'd booked a beach holiday, but there was a storm the whole week. So we hired a car and explored the mountains instead. Honestly, it was better than the beach would have been.

ask.s: How does he feel about the holiday?
ask.zh: 他對這次假期有什麼感覺？
ask.en: How does he feel about the holiday?

options.t: disappointed by the weather
pleased with how it turned out
sorry that he hired a car

explain.zh: 「比待在海灘還好」：結果令他滿意。
explain.en: Better than the beach would have been.

lines.s: You hear two students talking about a group project.
lines.zh: 你聽到兩個學生談小組作業。
lines.en: You hear two students talking about a group project.

lines.s: I've done my part. Has Jack finished his yet?
lines.zh: 我的部分做完了。傑克的做完了嗎？
lines.en: I've done my part. Has Jack finished his yet?

lines.s: He says he'll do it tonight, but he said that last week.
lines.zh: 他說今晚會做，可是上週他也這樣說。
lines.en: He says he'll do it tonight, but he said that last week.

lines.s: Then we should tell the teacher.
lines.zh: 那我們應該跟老師說。
lines.en: Then we should tell the teacher.

ask.s: What does the woman want to do?
ask.en: What does the woman want to do?

options.t: report the problem to the teacher
do Jack's work themselves
give Jack more time

explain.zh: 「那我們應該跟老師說」。

lines.s: You hear a woman talking about her new bicycle.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士談她的新腳踏車。
lines.en: You hear a woman talking about her new bicycle.

lines.s: It wasn't cheap, and I was worried I'd regret it. But I've used it every day for three months, and I've already saved more on bus fares than it cost.
lines.zh: 它不便宜，我還擔心會後悔。可是三個月來我每天騎，省下的公車錢已經超過車價了。
lines.en: It wasn't cheap, and I was worried I'd regret it. But I've used it every day for three months, and I've already saved more on bus fares than it cost.

ask.s: What does she say about the bike?
ask.en: What does she say about the bike?

options.t: She regrets buying it.
It was cheaper than she expected.
It has already paid for itself.

explain.zh: 「省下的公車錢已經超過車價了」：已經回本。
explain.en: The bus fares saved are more than it cost.

lines.s: Hello, I'm Dan Price, and I run Riverside Radio, a community station run entirely by volunteers. We started in a garage twelve years ago, and now we broadcast from the old fire station in the town centre. We've got about sixty volunteers; the youngest is fourteen and the oldest is eighty-seven. Our most popular programme is the Sunday morning show, where listeners phone in with gardening questions. Surprisingly, the show with the most younger listeners is one about local history. Every new volunteer starts by working on the news desk, because that teaches you to write clearly and quickly. Training takes about six weeks. The station is paid for by local businesses, who pay to have their adverts read out. The biggest challenge we face is finding people to work at night. This year we're celebrating our anniversary with a live concert in the park in July. And if you'd like to get involved, you don't need any experience — just enthusiasm.
lines.zh: 大家好，我是丹·普萊斯，經營河畔電台，一個完全由志工經營的社區電台。我們十二年前從一間車庫起家，現在在市中心的舊消防局播音。我們大約有六十位志工，最年輕的十四歲，最年長的八十七歲。最受歡迎的節目是星期天早上的節目，聽眾打電話進來問園藝問題。出乎意料的是，年輕聽眾最多的節目是講地方歷史的。每位新志工都從新聞台開始，因為那能訓練你寫得清楚又快。訓練大約要六週。電台的經費來自當地商家，他們付錢請我們播他們的廣告。我們最大的挑戰是找人值夜班。今年我們七月會在公園辦一場現場音樂會慶祝週年。想參與的話，不需要任何經驗，只要有熱情。
lines.en: Hello, I'm Dan Price, and I run Riverside Radio, a community station run entirely by volunteers. We started in a garage twelve years ago, and now we broadcast from the old fire station in the town centre. We've got about sixty volunteers; the youngest is fourteen and the oldest is eighty-seven. Our most popular programme is the Sunday morning show, where listeners phone in with gardening questions. Surprisingly, the show with the most younger listeners is one about local history. Every new volunteer starts by working on the news desk, because that teaches you to write clearly and quickly. Training takes about six weeks. The station is paid for by local businesses, who pay to have their adverts read out. The biggest challenge we face is finding people to work at night. This year we're celebrating our anniversary with a live concert in the park in July. And if you'd like to get involved, you don't need any experience — just enthusiasm.

ask.en: New volunteers start on the ＿＿＿＿＿ desk.

explain.zh: 「每位新志工都從新聞台開始」。

ask.en: Training takes about ＿＿＿＿＿.

explain.zh: 「訓練大約要六週」。

ask.s: The station is paid for by local ＿＿＿＿＿.
ask.en: The station is paid for by local ＿＿＿＿＿.

explain.zh: 「經費來自當地商家」。

ask.s: It is hardest to find people to work at ＿＿＿＿＿.
ask.en: It is hardest to find people to work at ＿＿＿＿＿.

explain.zh: 「最大的挑戰是找人值夜班」。

ask.s: The anniversary will be celebrated with a ＿＿＿＿＿ in the park.
ask.zh: 週年會在公園辦一場＿＿慶祝。
ask.en: The anniversary will be celebrated with a ＿＿＿＿＿ in the park.

explain.zh: 「在公園辦一場現場音樂會」。

lines.s: Speaker 1
lines.zh: 說話者 1
lines.en: Speaker 1

lines.s: I was sitting next to an old man on a train, and we started chatting. When I told him I was unhappy in my job, he said, 'Life's too short to wait for Friday.' I never even learnt his name, but I handed in my notice a month later.
lines.zh: 有一次火車上我坐在一位老先生旁邊，我們聊了起來。我說我工作不開心，他說：「人生太短，不該只為了等星期五。」我連他的名字都不知道，但一個月後我就遞了辭呈。
lines.en: I was sitting next to an old man on a train, and we started chatting. When I told him I was unhappy in my job, he said, 'Life's too short to wait for Friday.' I never even learnt his name, but I handed in my notice a month later.

lines.s: Speaker 2
lines.zh: 說話者 2
lines.en: Speaker 2

lines.s: My first manager told me to deal with the hardest task first thing every morning. Now I never start the day by checking emails. It's made me far more productive.
lines.zh: 我的第一個主管叫我每天早上先處理最難的工作。現在我從不一早就先看信，效率高多了。
lines.en: My first manager told me to deal with the hardest task first thing every morning. Now I never start the day by checking emails. It's made me far more productive.

lines.s: Speaker 3
lines.zh: 說話者 3
lines.en: Speaker 3

lines.s: When my father died, a friend told me to write down one good thing every evening, however small. Some days it was just 'the coffee was nice', but it kept me going through those months.
lines.zh: 我父親過世時，一個朋友叫我每天晚上寫下一件好事，再小都好。有些天只寫得出「咖啡很好喝」，但它讓我撐過了那幾個月。
lines.en: When my father died, a friend told me to write down one good thing every evening, however small. Some days it was just 'the coffee was nice', but it kept me going through those months.

lines.s: Speaker 4
lines.zh: 說話者 4
lines.en: Speaker 4

lines.s: My aunt kept saying I should learn to drive. I laughed — I lived in the city, why would I need a car? Then I got a job in the countryside, and suddenly I understood.
lines.zh: 我阿姨一直說我應該學開車。我都笑她，我住在城市，要車幹嘛？後來我在鄉下找到工作，突然就懂了。
lines.en: My aunt kept saying I should learn to drive. I laughed — I lived in the city, why would I need a car? Then I got a job in the countryside, and suddenly I understood.

lines.s: Speaker 5
lines.zh: 說話者 5
lines.en: Speaker 5

lines.s: A teacher once told me to listen more than I talk. I was a terrible listener. Since I started really trying, my friendships have got much closer, and my wife says I'm easier to live with.
lines.zh: 有位老師曾叫我多聽少說。我以前很不會聽人說話。自從我真的開始努力，我的友誼更親密了，太太也說我比較好相處了。
lines.en: A teacher once told me to listen more than I talk. I was a terrible listener. Since I started really trying, my friendships have got much closer, and my wife says I'm easier to live with.

lines.s: My guest is Maya Collins, who spent a year as the cook at a research station in Antarctica. Maya, why did you apply?
lines.zh: 今天的來賓是瑪雅·柯林斯，她在南極一個研究站當了一年廚師。瑪雅，你為什麼去應徵？
lines.en: My guest is Maya Collins, who spent a year as the cook at a research station in Antarctica. Maya, why did you apply?

lines.s: I'd been running a busy restaurant in London for ten years, and I was exhausted. I saw the advert on a friend's social media and thought: that's the opposite of my life. I applied the same evening.
lines.zh: 我在倫敦經營一家很忙的餐廳十年了，累壞了。我在朋友的社群上看到徵人廣告，心想：那跟我的生活完全相反。當天晚上我就應徵了。
lines.en: I'd been running a busy restaurant in London for ten years, and I was exhausted. I saw the advert on a friend's social media and thought: that's the opposite of my life. I applied the same evening.

lines.s: What was the biggest challenge in the kitchen?
lines.zh: 在廚房裡最大的挑戰是什麼？
lines.en: What was the biggest challenge in the kitchen?

lines.s: Planning. Fresh supplies arrive once a year, on a ship, so I had to work out exactly how much flour, rice and tinned food twenty people would need for twelve months. If I got it wrong, there was no shop to run to.
lines.zh: 規劃。補給一年才來一次，用船運來，所以我得精確算出二十個人十二個月要多少麵粉、米和罐頭。算錯了，可沒有商店可以跑。
lines.en: Planning. Fresh supplies arrive once a year, on a ship, so I had to work out exactly how much flour, rice and tinned food twenty people would need for twelve months. If I got it wrong, there was no shop to run to.

lines.s: What about fresh vegetables?
lines.zh: 那新鮮蔬菜呢？
lines.en: What about fresh vegetables?

lines.s: We had a small greenhouse with lights, and I grew lettuce and herbs. Nothing tastes as good as a salad in the middle of the Antarctic winter.
lines.zh: 我們有一間有燈的小溫室，我在裡面種萵苣和香草。在南極的冬天吃一盤沙拉，沒有什麼比這更美味了。
lines.en: We had a small greenhouse with lights, and I grew lettuce and herbs. Nothing tastes as good as a salad in the middle of the Antarctic winter.

lines.s: How did people cope with the dark months?
lines.zh: 大家怎麼度過那幾個月的黑暗？
lines.en: How did people cope with the dark months?

lines.s: Routine was everything. Having meals at exactly the same times became really important — it gave the day a shape. I also started a weekly 'restaurant night' where everyone dressed up, and it became the highlight of the week.
lines.zh: 規律就是一切。每天固定時間吃飯變得非常重要，讓一天有個樣子。我還辦了每週一次的「餐廳之夜」，大家都盛裝打扮，那成了一週的高潮。
lines.en: Routine was everything. Having meals at exactly the same times became really important — it gave the day a shape. I also started a weekly 'restaurant night' where everyone dressed up, and it became the highlight of the week.

lines.s: Was there anything you didn't enjoy?
lines.zh: 有什麼是你不喜歡的嗎？
lines.en: Was there anything you didn't enjoy?

lines.s: Honestly, the lack of privacy. You can't go for a walk on your own when it's minus forty. That was harder than the cold.
lines.zh: 老實說是沒有隱私。零下四十度的時候，你沒辦法一個人去散步。那比寒冷還難熬。
lines.en: Honestly, the lack of privacy. You can't go for a walk on your own when it's minus forty. That was harder than the cold.

lines.s: And now?
lines.zh: 那現在呢？
lines.en: And now?

lines.s: I've opened a small café rather than another big restaurant. I learnt that I'm happier cooking for people I know.
lines.zh: 我開了一家小咖啡館，而不是再開一家大餐廳。我發現為認識的人做菜，我比較快樂。
lines.en: I've opened a small café rather than another big restaurant. I learnt that I'm happier cooking for people I know.

ask.s: Why did Maya apply for the job?
ask.en: Why did Maya apply for the job?

options.t: She wanted a complete change from her life.
A friend asked her to apply.
She had always wanted to see Antarctica.

explain.zh: 累壞了，覺得那份工作「跟我的生活完全相反」。
explain.en: It was the opposite of her exhausting life.

ask.s: What does she say was hardest about cooking there?
ask.zh: 她說在那裡做菜最難的是什麼？
ask.en: What does she say was hardest about cooking there?

options.t: the lack of equipment
planning food for a whole year
cooking for so many people

explain.zh: 最大的挑戰是「規劃」：算出二十人一年的食物。

ask.s: How did she get fresh vegetables?
ask.en: How did she get fresh vegetables?

options.t: They arrived by ship.
She did without them.
She grew them indoors.

explain.zh: 「有燈的小溫室」裡種萵苣和香草。
explain.en: In a small greenhouse with lights.

ask.s: What helped people during the dark months?
ask.zh: 什麼幫大家度過黑暗的月份？
ask.en: What helped people during the dark months?

options.t: regular routines
long walks
phone calls home

explain.zh: 「規律就是一切」，固定時間吃飯讓一天有樣子。

ask.s: What was 'restaurant night'?
ask.en: What was 'restaurant night'?

options.t: a chance to cook for visitors
a weekly event where people dressed up
a competition between cooks

explain.zh: 「每週一次」、「大家都盛裝打扮」。

ask.s: What did Maya find most difficult?
ask.zh: 瑪雅覺得最難熬的是什麼？
ask.en: What did Maya find most difficult?

options.t: the cold
being alone
never having time to herself

explain.zh: 「沒有隱私」，沒辦法一個人去散步，「比寒冷還難熬」。
explain.en: No privacy — harder than the cold.

ask.s: What has she done since returning?
ask.en: What has she done since returning?

options.t: opened another large restaurant
opened a smaller business
stopped cooking

explain.zh: 「開了一家小咖啡館，而不是再開一家大餐廳」。
explain.en: A small café, not a big restaurant.
